label: Deploy: where each target lives, how many releases to keep, how long to wait for health

params.name: targets
params.label: Each target: its folder (repo, releases/, current, data/), service, service user, live port, probe port (the new release is tried here before the switch), branch, other units restarted onto the same code

params.name: default_target
params.label: Target used when none is named

params.name: keep_releases
params.label: Release folders kept (the live one and the one before it are never removed)

params.name: health_path
params.label: The address that must answer before and after the switch

params.name: health_wait_s
params.label: Seconds to wait for the health answer

params.name: probe
params.label: Start the new release on the probe port, with an empty data folder, and ask its health before the switch

params.name: requirements
params.label: Python packages: the first of these files that exists is installed (a lock file wins)

params.name: check_requirements
params.label: Packages the selfcheck needs (the quality gate's ruff, mypy, pip-audit), installed into the same venv when the file exists

params.name: selfcheck
params.label: Command run inside the new release before the switch; a non-zero exit keeps the live release

params.name: start_cmd
params.label: How the probe starts a release (the systemd unit uses the same line)

params.name: restart_cmd
params.label: How the live service is restarted onto the new release (sudo -n is added when not root)

params.name: python
params.label: Python used to build release venvs

description_nl: 2026-11-11 W1.4 (B10 deploy you can undo): deploy/deploy.sh reads this chip (env DEPLOY_<NAME> wins for one run). New code goes to releases/<commit>; the selfcheck and the probe health run before the current link moves; a failed live health moves it back; deploy.sh rollback goes to the release before. 2026-11-12: staging 8837 (8836 is valuefy on the VPS); check_requirements = the selfcheck's own tools (W1.3 gate failed the first server deploy without ruff).
